items.title: Relief materials provided to flood-affected families in Rasuwa
items.summary: Kathmandu, October 7 Relief materials have been provided to 60 flood-affected households at Dandagaun of Uttargaya Rural Municipality-2 in Rasuwa. The materials were distributed through the Integrated Humanitarian and Early Recovery Programme with support from Start Fund Nepal, according to Lubh Raj Neupane, executive director of Rural-Oriented Youth Movement (ROYM) Nepal. items.title: Flood cuts off market access for Rasuwa farmers as vegetables pile up
items.summary: Farmers in Gatlang had expanded cultivation after strong returns last year, but damaged roads and bridges now threaten to leave this year’s harvest rotting in the fields.

items.title: Flood-hit districts remain cut off from national road network
items.summary: Repairs are underway in Manang, Mustang, Baglung and Rasuwa, but damaged bridges and approach roads continue to disrupt direct road links.

items.title: Nepal’s growth to slow to 3.7 percent after devastating Rasuwa flood
items.summary: The World Bank estimates $1.66 billion in direct damage to physical assets, with infrastructure accounting for 83 percent of the losses.

items.title: Nepal’s disaster panel is debating what to call the Bhotekoshi floods. ‘Himalayan tsunami’ isn’t on the list
items.summary: Prime Minister Balendra Shah used the term at the UN, but experts on the government panel say they are considering other names for the August 26 disaster.
